title: 1973 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Define \(n_a!\) for positive \(n\) and \(a\) to be \[ \begin{aligned} n_a!={}&n(n-a)(n-2a)\\ &\cdot(n-3a)\cdots(n-ka), \end{aligned} \] where \(k\) is the greatest integer for which \(n\gt ka.\) Then the quotient \[ \frac{72_8!}{18_2!} \] is equal to

solutions.text:
The two products are \[ \begin{aligned} 72_8!&=72\cdot64\cdots8 =8^9(9!),\\ 18_2!&=18\cdot16\cdots2 =2^9(9!). \end{aligned} \] Their quotient is therefore \[ \frac{8^9(9!)}{2^9(9!)}=4^9. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
